notes:
Map quality vs trainer rules: very good. All internal relationships are [U,S,PL]->[D,C,ACL] (C/S between internal teams, ACL default, PL upstream); no Shared Kernel (comment cites expert's 'no shared database or library'); Conformist only to Stripe, justified as industry-standard; VideoProvider -> LessonDelivery ACL. Complaints is placed downstream of Trust & Safety and Billing (speaking their intake language), which avoids a T&S->Scheduling->Complaints->T&S cycle and the direction was confirmed by the expert. Subdomain classification (core = Trust + Reviews) included. Canvases created, no code. Mechanical grading all green.

Kept indirect cycle (Pricing -> Scheduling -> LessonDelivery (-> Reviews) -> Pricing): the justification (slow business feedback loop, each arrow a different concept, documented in CML) is defensible but not fully convincing. An acyclic alternative existed and was not considered: make LessonDelivery an OHS service that Scheduling calls to set up/move/cancel sessions (LessonDelivery upstream of Scheduling), which is exactly how the baseline run broke the same loop with expert confirmation. The 'alternatives rejected' list only covers counting from Billing and a Pricing intake API. The skill applied the 'downstream speaks upstream's intake API' trick for Complaints but not to Scheduling->LessonDelivery. Suggest the skill instruct: before keeping a cycle, enumerate flipping each edge in the cycle (incl. 'callee offers OHS API') and ask the expert about the cheapest one. Also, the critic final pass approved the cycle; the critic should be prompted to propose concrete edge flips.

Over-engineering / drift from facts: many decisions rest on [improvised] answers the facilitator's questions elicited: Student Accounts gets a 'student block' decision (unpaid lessons), Payouts owns the earnings ledger, Billing reports payment-guarantee into Scheduling's API, Trust & Safety -> Payouts TutorCountry. Each is reasonable but the map becomes larger than the ground truth needs; questions in rounds 2-4 drilled into edge cases (pre-auth failure, collections, suspended tutor payouts) that do not change boundaries. The skill could cap rounds or prioritise questions that move a boundary. Also an open contradiction is surfaced ('commission added on top vs deducted') - good.

Cost: 7 expert rounds, ~255k tokens, ~20 min vs baseline ~79k tokens / ~4 min (3.2x tokens, 4.9x time). The value is real (critic caught the 50% triple ownership and a hidden-cycle assumption) but the per-context critic round plus per-process map critics plus final pass is heavy for a 9-context system; consider batching per-context critics into one call and only re-running DISAGREE ones (it already does the latter).

Eval critique: assertions 1-4 are passed by the baseline too, so they don't discriminate; the discriminating outcomes are relationship patterns (C/S+ACL vs CF) and cycle handling, which only mechanical checks partly cover. Consider adding: 'internal relationships are Customer/Supplier with ACL downstream (no CF to internal contexts)' and 'no U/D cycle, or a kept cycle is justified after considering flipping each edge'.
